meta.description: Analyzes base-editing screens for variant function: library design (Hanna 2021 ClinVar-scale CBE screen, Cuella-Martin 2021 DDR saturation), CBE vs ABE chemistry choice, editing-window math (positions 4-8 from PAM-distal end), bystander-edit quantification, sgRNA-efficiency filtering before hit calling, indel byproduct interpretation, ClinVar/COSMIC annotation, and the Broad be-validation-pipeline.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated statistics, DOIs, or trial results. Editing-window values, thresholds, and the Hanna/Cuella-Martin methodology descriptions match the cited primary literature.

practice_boundaries.detail: Research-scope screen/variant-function analysis only; no diagnostic or prescriptive claims about a person or patient.

methodological_ground.detail: Editing-window math, chemistry selection logic, and the substitution-vs-indel diagnostic are methodologically sound; the diagnostic was independently confirmed correct on a real, ground-truth-known Cas9 sample (ratio 0.12, correctly called Cas9-like against the Skill's own <3 threshold).

code_usability.detail: All three of the Skill's data-integration Python functions crash immediately when run against real tool output: filter_by_editing_efficiency() raises KeyError 'Position' against a real CRISPResso2 Quantification_window_nucleotide_percentage_table.txt (the function assumes rows=Position/columns=base; the real file is the transpose, rows=base/columns=position). deconvolute_bystander() raises KeyError 'Reference_pct' against a real Alleles_frequency_table.zip (the real column is '%Reads'). aggregate_variant_scores() raises KeyError 'sgRNA' merging against a real MAGeCK sgrna_summary.txt (the real column is lowercase 'sgrna'). The fourth function, find_be_spacers(), does not crash but silently misattributes target-vs-bystander classification for any reverse-strand candidate: it computes genomic_pos in reverse-complement coordinate space but compares it against forward-strand codon boundaries, producing a confirmed false on-target call for a spacer whose actual edited base lies 65nt away from the intended codon.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness is strong (library design through hit-calling integration, case studies, decision rules). Correctness docked hard: 3 of 4 bundled functions crash on real tool output and the 4th silently misattributes coordinates on the reverse strand, all confirmed by execution.

reliability.note: No schema validation or column-existence checks in any bundled function. The Version-Compatibility note only tells the agent to recover from ImportError/AttributeError/TypeError -- none of the four real failures found were those types (three are KeyError from wrong assumed schema, one is a silent coordinate error), so the stated recovery path does not cover the actual failure modes.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md ~360 lines with usage-guide.md and examples/ split out; some chemistry/threshold table duplication between the two docs, same pattern as the sibling crispresso-editing Skill.

agent_usability.note: Strong learnability and mostly-consistent decision trees. Feedback Design and Error Prevention both docked hard: no function checks its input schema before indexing into it, and the one function that doesn't crash (find_be_spacers) gives no signal at all that its reverse-strand output can be wrong.

human_usability.note: Natural, well-targeted trigger prompts throughout usage-guide.md. Forgiveness is weak: a researcher who runs the bundled code has no documented way to notice the silent coordinate bug, and the three crashes have no recovery guidance beyond the generic version-compatibility note.

security.note: No secrets or injection vectors; inputs are sequence strings, file paths, and column names. Minor: no input-range validation (e.g., target_aa, target_base) and no mention of clinical-sample sensitivity.

maintainability.note: Clean SKILL.md/usage-guide.md/examples split. Testability docked to 0/4: none of the four bundled functions show evidence of having been run against real CRISPResso2 or MAGeCK output before shipping -- all four have defects that a single real test run would have caught.

agent_specific.note: Precise, detailed triggering and excellent Related-Skills composability across the whole CRISPR-screen family. Escape Hatches docked: no guidance for what an agent should do when a bundled function crashes on real data, or how to independently verify a function's output before trusting it (as this audit had to do for find_be_spacers).

inputs.label: CBE saturation library design tiling a target region (find_be_spacers, BE4max)
inputs.note: Ran verbatim on a synthetic 300nt CDS (100 codons, seeded, no stop codons). Completed without error, found 21 candidate spacers, 1 flagged on-target for aa 40 -- but that hit is a reverse-strand spacer, and independent coordinate verification shows the code compares a reverse-complement-space index (117) directly against forward-strand codon bounds [117,120) without ever converting back; the base actually being edited sits at true forward-CDS index 182, 65nt from the intended codon. A researcher trusting this output would misassign an off-target edit as on-target with no warning.

assertions.note: Confirmed: loops over forward CDS and its reverse complement.

assertions.text: On-target hits reported by the function are genuinely within the intended codon
assertions.note: The one on-target hit found is a reverse-strand candidate whose true edited base is 65nt outside the target codon; confirmed by independent coordinate math.

assertions.text: No silent, unflagged coordinate error for reverse-strand candidates
assertions.note: genomic_pos is computed in reverse-complement index space but compared against forward-strand codon boundaries with no conversion.

assertions.text: Function completes without raising an exception on a realistic synthetic CDS
assertions.note: Ran to completion, returned a well-formed, sorted DataFrame.

inputs.label: Editing-efficiency filtering on real CRISPResso2 pilot output (filter_by_editing_efficiency)
inputs.note: Ran verbatim against real CRISPResso2 2.3.4 output from this audit's synthetic CBE FASTQ (ground truth: 50% target editing, 30% bystander editing, planted). Crashed immediately: KeyError 'Position'. The function assumes the quantification-window table has a 'Position' column with base-percentage columns; the real file is the transpose (rows are A/C/G/T/N/-, columns are per-window-position reference bases, duplicated column names). This is the same class of defect (assumed-vs-real file schema mismatch) already found as a P0 in the sibling crispresso-editing Skill's audit.

assertions.note: KeyError: 'Position', reproduced directly against the real file.

assertions.text: The function's assumed table orientation (rows=Position, columns=base) matches the real file
assertions.note: Real file: rows=A/C/G/T/N/-, columns=per-position reference base (duplicated names); the file is the transpose of what the code assumes.

assertions.text: The editing-efficiency threshold convention (>=30% primary, >=50% validation) is methodologically sound
assertions.note: Matches the field convention documented and is internally consistent with the Skill's own Quantitative Thresholds table.

assertions.text: Failure is a loud exception rather than a silently wrong number
assertions.note: KeyError halts execution rather than returning a plausible-looking but incorrect editing percentage.

inputs.label: ABE7.10 zero-bystander spacer search for a single-variant install (find_be_spacers, target_base='A')
inputs.note: Ran on the same synthetic CDS with editor='ABE7.10', target_base='A'. Completed, found 20 candidates, 0 with target_positions non-empty AND n_bystanders==0 -- consistent with the Skill's own documented fallback ('if no zero-bystander spacer exists, list candidates sorted by bystander_count and recommend prime editor'). The ABE7.10 window dict value (4,7) matches SKILL.md's own table exactly. The same reverse-strand coordinate bug from Input 1 remains latent in this code path (no on-target hit happened to surface here, but nothing in the function would have caught it if one had).

inputs.label: Bystander deconvolution from a real CRISPResso2 allele-frequency table (deconvolute_bystander)
inputs.note: Ran verbatim against the real Alleles_frequency_table.zip from the same synthetic CBE run. Crashed: KeyError 'Reference_pct' -- the real column is '%Reads'. Patching only that one column name and re-running recovers the exact planted ground truth: 40.0% unmodified, 30.0% target-only, 20.0% target+bystander, 10.0% bystander-only, matching the four planted read populations exactly. The underlying position-indexing logic is correct; only the column name is wrong.

inputs.label: BE-Hive editing-efficiency prediction for a designed guide, following only the Skill's guidance
inputs.note: The Skill gives one sentence on BE-Hive ('clone maxwshen/be_predict_bystander and import via sys.path') with zero code and no mention of its required 50nt-substrate convention or its own internal 1-indexed position numbering. Built the substrate by hand per BE-Hive's own README; a first attempt used the README's literal '-19 to 30' arithmetic and was off by one nucleotide relative to BE-Hive's actual internal indexing (confirmed via its own 'Assumed protospacer sequence' diagnostic field). Once reconciled, init_model(BE4, mES) + predict() ran to completion (Total predicted probability 0.98) and correctly identified both planted editable C's (this audit's target and bystander positions) as the dominant variable columns in the output.

recommendations.title: filter_by_editing_efficiency() crashes on real CRISPResso2 output
recommendations.problem: The function raises KeyError: 'Position' on the first real Quantification_window_nucleotide_percentage_table.txt it is run against -- the exact 'non-negotiable' filtering step the usage-guide calls critical.
recommendations.root_cause: The code assumes rows=Position/columns=base-percentage; the real CRISPResso2 file is the transpose (rows=A/C/G/T/N/-, columns=per-window-position reference base, with duplicated column names).
recommendations.fix: Rewrite to read the file with index_col=0, transpose it (or iterate columns instead of a 'Position' column), and pull the position via the table's column order rather than a nonexistent 'Position' field. Verify against a real CRISPResso2 output directory before shipping.

recommendations.title: deconvolute_bystander() crashes on real CRISPResso2 allele tables
recommendations.problem: The function raises KeyError: 'Reference_pct' on a real Alleles_frequency_table.zip.
recommendations.fix: Change the groupby aggregation column to '%Reads'. The rest of the function is correct as written -- confirmed it recovers planted ground truth exactly (40/30/20/10) once this one name is fixed.

recommendations.title: aggregate_variant_scores() crashes merging against real MAGeCK output
recommendations.problem: The function raises KeyError: 'sgRNA' merging mageck_sgrna_summary with variant_annotation_df.
recommendations.root_cause: Real MAGeCK sgrna_summary.txt uses the lowercase column name 'sgrna', not 'sgRNA'.
recommendations.fix: Merge on 'sgrna' (or normalize both frames' column names to a common case before merging) and document the real MAGeCK column name in the Hit Calling section.

recommendations.title: find_be_spacers() silently misattributes target/bystander for reverse-strand spacers
recommendations.problem: For minus-strand candidates, the function computes genomic_pos in reverse-complement coordinate space but compares it directly against forward-strand codon boundaries with no conversion. A confirmed on-target call in this audit's test run was actually 65nt from the intended codon. This produces no error and no warning -- a researcher would trust a wrong on-target call.
recommendations.root_cause: Missing coordinate conversion (true_forward_index = len(cds_sequence) - 1 - genomic_pos) for the strand == '-' branch before comparing against target_codon_start/target_codon_end.
recommendations.fix: Convert genomic_pos back to forward-CDS coordinates for minus-strand candidates before the codon-overlap check, and add a unit test with a known reverse-strand hit to catch regressions.

recommendations.title: BE-Hive integration has no code sample and omits its position-numbering convention
recommendations.problem: The Skill names BE-Hive as its efficiency-prediction tool in one sentence with no worked example, no mention of the required 50nt-substrate layout, and no warning that BE-Hive's internal 1-indexed position numbering can be offset from a naive construction of that substrate.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill treats BE-Hive as a citation rather than an integration point, unlike its detailed treatment of CRISPResso2 CLI flags.
recommendations.fix: Add a short worked BE-Hive code example (init_model + predict on a concrete sequence) and a note to cross-check BE-Hive's own 'Assumed protospacer sequence' diagnostic field against the intended spacer before trusting its position-labeled output columns.

recommendations.title: No bundled function validates its input schema before indexing into it
recommendations.problem: All four bundled functions index directly into an assumed column/schema with no existence check, so every one of the three real-data integration points fails with an unhelpful KeyError instead of a clear, actionable error.
recommendations.root_cause: None of the four functions appear to have been run against real CRISPResso2 or MAGeCK output before being included in the Skill.
recommendations.fix: Add a schema assertion (e.g., assert 'Position' in df.columns, f'unexpected columns: {list(df.columns)}') at the top of each function so a future schema drift fails loudly and specifically rather than with a bare KeyError.

recommendations.title: Chemistry and threshold tables duplicated between SKILL.md and usage-guide.md
recommendations.problem: The Base Editor Chemistry Selection table and the editing-efficiency threshold convention both appear near-verbatim in both files with no cross-reference.
recommendations.root_cause: The two files were not consolidated to a single source of truth when split.
recommendations.fix: Keep the full table in one file and reference it from the other, as already done cleanly for the Related Skills section.
